hook.text: Hello and welcome to Jira Product Discovery. Here's a quick demo on how it works.

cta.text: Please make sure to join our community for news about product and practices

summary.tone: Casual, first-person product-manager walkthrough: friendly and practical, unscripted-sounding narration over a raw screen recording, tutorial rather than marketing

signature_moments.description: Digital punch-in crops onto the active UI region at each narrated step (idea row, field panel, Sales list, timeline), easing back to the full browser between features.
signature_moments.why_premium: Directs the eye in a dense UI without any designed overlays; it is the main attention device in an otherwise raw recording, though the reframes are abrupt rather than finely eased.

signature_moments.description: Highlighting a passage in a third-party article and attaching it to an idea through the Chrome extension popup.
signature_moments.why_premium: Shows the product reaching outside its own app in one continuous, believable action, which makes the capture-insights benefit concrete.

signature_moments.description: The cursor hovers the 'community' link in the feedback modal exactly as the VO says 'join our community' (w563-w565).
signature_moments.why_premium: A small voice-to-picture sync that grounds the call to action in the real UI instead of a generic end card.

hook.evidence: Generic greeting plus a promise of a quick demo (w0-w14) over a fade-up into an unannotated product list; no problem, stakes or claim to earn attention.

clarity.evidence: Clear capture, prioritise, share, deliver progression; each feature is named in the VO while the cursor performs it (e.g. delivery ticket creation w504-w541), and punch-ins point at the active area. Small full-frame UI text and the 177 s length dilute it slightly.

ui_showcase.evidence: Real product with realistic data across list, board, timeline, matrix and delivery views, but shown as a raw browser capture with URL bar, extensions and avatar visible, tiny text at full frame and no recreated or emphasized UI.

motion_polish.evidence: Motion is limited to cursor activity and digital crop punch-ins; reframes are abrupt (s003 transition is an abrupt reframe), shots join with hard cuts/jump cuts, and the video ends on a static UI frame with no designed transitions, type or end card.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchor audio facts plus visuals: integrated loudness is low at -24.64 LUFS, only two SFX candidates in 177 s (x001 unsure at 45.09 s; x002 swoosh_reverse at 135.13 s, which lines up with the timeline punch-in in s004), and a 126 BPM beat grid is detected but I cannot confirm from anchors whether a music bed is present. Sound is essentially the voice-over.

vo_script_quality.evidence: Conversational and accurate with good feature-to-benefit lines ('quick wins or big bets', w284-w289), but loose and unscripted-sounding: repeated 'Now' openers including a stumble (w357-w358), filler like 'or better again' (w161-w163), and a flat 'OK, that's it' outro (w556-w558).

brand_consistency.evidence: Everything on screen is the consistent Atlassian product UI, but there is no branded intro, title card, lockup or end card; the brand appears only in the app header.

works_muted.evidence: No captions or overlay text; muted, a viewer sees UI clicks but loses why each view matters and the CTA (w559-w571) exists only in the VO.

overall.evidence: A competent, clear narrated product tutorial with sensible structure and good VO-action sync, but tutorial-grade production: weak hook, raw capture, minimal motion and sound design, no muted support and no designed ending.

localization_friendliness.notes: No overlay captions to translate, so re-voicing plus subtitles is straightforward, but the meaning rests on the English VO and the product UI itself (labels, sample data, the Medium article) is baked into the recording in English and would need re-capturing for a fully localized version.
